room.spatial_character: A compact single-person office with an east-side work position, north storage, and a separate window-adjacent reading place.
daily_activities: short reading away from the workstation
room.organization: The desk and chair occupy the east work strip. The north bookcase and south file cabinet keep storage on boundaries. The north-west armchair group receives daylight without occupying the window clearance, while the center remains a circulation and turning field.
room.main_path: Enter through the south-center door into the open center, then continue east to the desk chair, north to the bookcase, south-east to the file cabinet, or north-west to the reading chair.
room.protected_open_space: The area immediately north of the door and the central field between the reading chair and desk chair remain open so that desk-chair pull-out, storage access, and entry circulation do not overlap.

openings.placement_rationale: The south-center door enters an empty turn-in area, with the file cabinet set far to its east and no chair or table inside the inward clearance.
The north-west window lights the reading side of the office; the chair group remains below its interior clearance and the bookcase begins well east of the opening.

furniture.placement_rationale: The primary desk runs along the east wall and points west into the room, which gives its seated user an open view rather than a view into a wall. Its narrow depth leaves a dedicated chair and pull-out band to the west, while the desk's north and south ends stay clear of the bookcase and file cabinet access zones.

This chair faces desk_work_east from its west side with a deliberate gap for knees and chair movement. The pull-out direction is toward the central open field, not toward the south door or the north storage wall, so a user can stand up without interrupting the entry route.

The tall bookcase is held to the north wall east of the north-west window, keeping both the glazing clearance and the reading chair's daylight pocket open. Its south-facing retrieval side opens onto the central aisle and is separated from the desk corner, so browsing books does not require passing behind the work chair.

The low file cabinet uses the south-east wall away from the entry opening and remains close to the work desk for active papers. Its north-facing operating side has open floor in front of it, so drawers can be used without competing with the desk chair or door clearance.

The armchair creates a brief-reading place on the north-west side, close enough to benefit from the window but more than the window clearance depth away from the wall. Its diagonal orientation turns toward the central room and leaves a southeast approach from the entry path rather than forcing the reader to squeeze beside a wall.

The small side table sits at the armchair's north-east side for a book or drink, beyond the chair's diagonal approach edge. It stays below the north window clearance and leaves the direct south-east approach to armchair_window_reading untouched.

The slim floor lamp occupies the west-side pocket beside the reading chair, where it can light the seat without using the central walking field. Its small base remains clear of both the chair's south-east approach and the north window zone.
